title: Lordship, dignity and aspects
goal: Done when you can judge the dignity, relationships, functional nature, aspects and house placement of each of your 12 house lords, and justify each verdict with a source and one cross-check.

exaltation: The sign where a planet is strongest. BPHS gives the deepest point inside it: Sun 10° Aries, Moon 3° Taurus, Mars 28° Capricorn, Mercury 15° Virgo, Jupiter 5° Cancer, Venus 27° Pisces, Saturn 20° Libra.
debilitation: The sign opposite a planet’s exaltation, where it is weakest. The deepest fall point is the same degree as the deepest exaltation point, in the opposite sign.
moolatrikona: A stretch of one sign where a planet is treated as a little stronger than in the rest of its own sign. For the Sun it is Leo 0°–20°.
swakshetra: A sign ruled by the planet. The Sun and Moon own one sign each; the other five planets own two.
ucchabala: Exaltation strength: the planet’s angular distance from its deepest fall point, divided by 3, giving 0 to 60 virupas. It is the first part of Sthana bala in Shadbala (BPHS ch. 27).
maitri: The relationship between two planets: friend, neutral or enemy. It decides how comfortable a planet is in the other’s sign.
tatkalika: Temporary friendship, read from one chart: planets in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th from each other are friends; in the 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th or 9th they are enemies.
panchadha: The five-fold relationship: natural and temporary friendship combined into great friend, friend, neutral, enemy or great enemy.
grahayuddha: Two of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn within 1° of longitude. One planet is judged the winner and the other the loser; the loser is said to lose strength.
cheshta: Motional strength in Shadbala. A retrograde (vakra) planet gets the maximum, 60 virupas, in the BPHS scheme.
functional: A planet’s nature for one particular lagna, decided by the houses it rules, not by its natural nature. Jupiter is a natural benefic but can be a functional malefic.
yogakaraka: A planet that rules both a kendra and a trikona for a given lagna (for example Saturn for Libra lagna). The Parashari texts treat it as the most helpful planet for that lagna.
maraka: A planet tied to the 2nd and 7th houses, the houses that stand twelfth from the longevity houses 3 and 8. In practice it signals strain on vitality in its periods; it is not a death sentence.
kendradhipati: The blemish a natural benefic is said to take when it rules a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th). The lagna lord is excused.
drishti: Planetary aspect, the Parashari kind: every planet sees the 7th house; Mars also sees the 4th and 8th, Jupiter the 5th and 9th, Saturn the 3rd and 10th.
rashidrishti: Sign aspect, the Jaimini kind: movable signs see the fixed signs except the adjacent one, fixed signs see the movable signs except the adjacent one, dual signs see the other dual signs.
bhavesha: The planet that rules the sign on a house. Its own sign, house, dignity and company decide how that house delivers.
viparita: Success through reversal: the lord of the 6th, 8th or 12th sits in another of those three houses. Your Saturn, 6th lord in the 8th, forms the Harsha variety.
asta: Combustion. See also the Stage 1 term “combust”. The Sun’s closeness weakens a planet; the orb differs by planet.

lessons.title: Dignity in degrees: exaltation, moolatrikona, own sign
lessons.body:
Recall: Your Moon is in Pushya. Which planet’s mahadasha was running when you were born, and which sign is the Moon in?

In Stage 1 you graded a planet by its sign. Classical dignity is finer than that: it is measured in degrees. The same sign can hold a planet at its peak, at a good level, or merely at home, depending on how far into the sign it has travelled. This lesson gives you the degree map from BPHS chapter 3 and shows how to turn it into a number.

The degree map

PlanetDeepest exaltationDeepest fall (debilitation)MoolatrikonaRest of own sign
SunAries 10°Libra 10°Leo 0°–20°Leo 20°–30°
MoonTaurus 3°Scorpio 3°Taurus 3°–30°Cancer, all 30°
MarsCapricorn 28°Cancer 28°Aries 0°–12°Aries 12°–30°; Scorpio
MercuryVirgo 15°Pisces 15°Virgo 15°–20°Virgo 20°–30°; Gemini
JupiterCancer 5°Capricorn 5°Sagittarius 0°–10°Sagittarius 10°–30°; Pisces
VenusPisces 27°Virgo 27°Libra 0°–15°Libra 15°–30°; Taurus
SaturnLibra 20°Aries 20°Aquarius 0°–20°Aquarius 20°–30°; Capricorn

The rules behind the table, as BPHS ch. 3 (verses 49 to 54, in R. Santhanam’s translation) states them:

  • Each planet is {{term:exaltation|exalted}} in one sign and {{term:debilitation|debilitated}} in the sign opposite. The deepest point of each is the same degree.
  • Inside its own sign a planet may have a {{term:moolatrikona|moolatrikona}} stretch. Mercury is the clearest case: in Virgo the first 15° are the exaltation zone, the next 5° moolatrikona, the last 10° plain own sign.
  • Sun and Moon each own one sign. Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn each own two; only one of the two carries a moolatrikona stretch (Mars Aries, Mercury Virgo, Jupiter Sagittarius, Venus Libra, Saturn Aquarius).
  • The Moon’s exaltation zone (0°–3° Taurus) comes first and its moolatrikona is the rest of Taurus. Tables that count the first degree as “1°” print this as 4°–30°; it is the same stretch. The same convention prints Mercury’s Virgo stretch as 16°–20°.

Check your software. The engine behind this app labels “moolatrikona” by sign only, without testing the degree. A planet at 18° Virgo for Mercury is moolatrikona; at 25° Virgo it is only in its own sign. You apply the degree test yourself. None of your planets sits in a moolatrikona sign, so this does not change your chart.

The ladder, and what it is worth

BPHS ch. 3 verses 59 and 60 give the share of its good effects a planet can deliver. Translations word the verse slightly differently (the neutral-sign share is “very little” in some), but the ladder is conventionally taught like this:

Planet is inShare of full good effect
ExaltationFull
MoolatrikonaThree-quarters
Own signOne-half
Friend’s signOne-quarter
Neutral’s signOne-eighth
Enemy’s sign or debilitationNil (the inauspicious effects are the reverse of the above)

Shadbala later turns the same ladder into virupas: moolatrikona 45, own sign 30, great friend 20, friend 15, neutral 10, enemy 4, great enemy 2 (BPHS ch. 27 verses 2 to 4, as Santhanam renders them). Other Shadbala texts and most software use 22.5, 15, 7.5, 3.75 and 1.875 for the five friendship grades, so check which scale a printout uses. You will meet that in Stage 8.

A number for every degree: uccha bala

Exaltation is not an on/off switch. The closer a planet is to its deepest exaltation point, the stronger it is, and the closer to its deepest fall point, the weaker. BPHS ch. 27 verse 1 gives the formula:

  1. Take the planet’s longitude and subtract the longitude of its deepest fall point.
  2. If the answer is over 180°, subtract it from 360°.
  3. Divide by 3. The result is the strength in virupas, from 0 to 60.

Worked example, your Saturn. Deepest fall point: Aries 20°, which is longitude 20°. Saturn is at Aries 7°41′, longitude 7.69°. Distance 12.31°. Divide by 3: 4.1 virupas out of 60. Saturn is nearly at the bottom of its range.

Try the Moon. Deepest fall: Scorpio 3°, longitude 213°. The Moon is at Cancer 8°04′, longitude 98.07°. Distance 114.93°, under 180°, so divide by 3: 38.3 virupas. Check your own arithmetic against the table below.

In your chart

Your seven planets, with the dignity zone and the uccha bala from the engine’s longitudes:

PlanetPositionZoneUccha bala (of 60)
SunGemini 10°41′Gemini, Mercury’s sign (neutral by the natural table)39.8
MoonCancer 8°04′Cancer, own sign38.3
MarsTaurus 29°19′Taurus, Venus’s sign (neutral by the natural table)19.6
MercuryGemini 28°10′Gemini, own sign34.4
JupiterPisces 3°28′Pisces, own sign19.5
VenusTaurus 8°18′Taurus, own sign46.2
SaturnAries 7°41′Aries, debilitated; 12°19′ short of the deepest fall point4.1

Venus (46.2) is your strongest planet by this one measure and Saturn (4.1) your weakest. Notice what the number does not say: Saturn’s weakness is partly offset because its debilitation is cancelled ({{term:neechabhanga|neechabhanga}}), and Venus’s strength is only one component of Shadbala. Uccha bala is a first filter, not a verdict.

Where the schools differ
  • BPHS ranges (Santhanam’s translation): the table above. This is the standard Parashari reference.
  • Narrower moolatrikona ranges: some modern tables list shorter stretches (Sun 1°–10° and Moon 4°–20°). No verse source for them has been traced, so use the BPHS ranges unless your teacher says otherwise.
  • Rahu and Ketu: Santhanam notes that the texts hold different views on their exaltation. The most common pairs are Taurus and Scorpio, or Gemini and Sagittarius. Do not grade a node’s dignity until you know which your teacher uses.
  • Jaimini and KP: Jaimini uses exaltation and debilitation (for example in its raja yogas) but not this virupa ladder; it judges mainly through karakas and rashi aspects. KP does not use the ladder and judges through star lord and sub-lord.
Cross-check

Test a dignity call against the navamsa (D9): a planet strong in D1 and in D9 is more reliable. Your Mercury is vargottama (Gemini in both). Then test the ayanamsa. Under the Raman ayanamsa your Mars moves from Taurus 29°19′ to Gemini 0°46′, a change of sign and of dignity; under the KP ayanamsa it stays in Taurus (29°25′). A call that survives both is safer than one that flips.

Remember
  • Dignity is measured in degrees: exaltation point, moolatrikona stretch, plain own sign.
  • Uccha bala = (distance from the deepest fall point ÷ 3) virupas, maximum 60.
  • Check the degree yourself; some software labels moolatrikona by sign alone.
  • Your Saturn: 4.1 of 60. Your Venus: 46.2 of 60.

Practice: Compute the uccha bala for your Sun and your Mars by hand, using the deepest fall points in the table. Compare with 39.8 and 19.6. Then write one sentence on why Mars scoring 19.6 and being combust are two separate facts.
lessons.listen: Classical dignity is measured in degrees. Each planet has a deepest exaltation point: Sun ten degrees Aries, Moon three Taurus, Mars twenty eight Capricorn, Mercury fifteen Virgo, Jupiter five Cancer, Venus twenty seven Pisces and Saturn twenty Libra. The deepest fall point is the same degree in the opposite sign. Inside a planet’s own sign there may be a moolatrikona stretch: Sun Leo zero to twenty, Mars Aries zero to twelve, Mercury Virgo fifteen to twenty, Jupiter Sagittarius zero to ten, Venus Libra zero to fifteen, Saturn Aquarius zero to twenty, and the Moon in Taurus after its first three degrees. Uccha bala turns this into a number: take the distance from the deepest fall point and divide by three. Your Saturn, debilitated at seven degrees forty one minutes of Aries, scores only four point one virupas out of sixty. Your Venus scores forty six point two. Check the degree yourself, because some software labels moolatrikona by sign alone.
sources: BPHS ch. 3 (planetary characters and description), verses 49 to 54 on exaltation, debilitation and moolatrikona, and 59 to 60 on the share of effects; R. Santhanam’s translation numbering
BPHS ch. 27 (evaluation of strengths), verse 1 on uccha bala and verses 2 to 4 on saptavargaja values
Moon’s moolatrikona start and the narrower modern ranges: cross-checked against secondary tables only

quiz.q: Where is Jupiter’s deepest exaltation point?
quiz.w: BPHS ch. 3: Jupiter exalts in Cancer, deepest at 5°. Capricorn 5° is the deepest fall.

quiz.q: Mercury stands at 17° Virgo. Which zone is it in?
quiz.w: In Virgo Mercury has 15° of exaltation zone, then 5° of moolatrikona, then 10° of plain own sign.

quiz.q: Your Saturn is at Aries 7°41′ and its deepest fall point is Aries 20°. Its uccha bala is about…
quiz.w: (20° − 7.69°) ÷ 3 = 4.1. A planet near its deepest fall point scores close to zero.

quiz.q: In the BPHS ladder, a planet in its plain own sign gives about what share of its full good effect?
quiz.w: Exaltation full, moolatrikona three-quarters, own sign one-half, friend one-quarter.

lessons.title: Friends and enemies: natural, temporary and five-fold
lessons.body:
Recall: In which part of Virgo does Mercury have its moolatrikona, and how many degrees is that stretch?

A planet sitting in another planet’s sign is a guest in someone else’s house. Whether it is welcomed depends on {{term:maitri|friendship}}. Jyotish measures that friendship twice and then combines the two results. That is the five-fold relationship, taught in BPHS ch. 3.

Step 1: natural friendship (permanent)

The natural relationships do not depend on any chart. BPHS ch. 3 verse 55 supplies a rule that regenerates the whole table:

  1. Start from the planet’s moolatrikona sign.
  2. The lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th signs from it are its friends.
  3. The lords of the 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th signs are its enemies.
  4. The lord of its exaltation sign is always counted a friend.
  5. A planet counted as both friend and enemy becomes neutral. A planet not counted at all is neutral.

Worked example, Mars. Moolatrikona Aries. Signs 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12 from Aries are Taurus, Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Pisces, lords Venus, Moon, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Jupiter. Signs 3, 6, 7, 10, 11 are Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn, Aquarius, lords Mercury, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Saturn. The exaltation sign Capricorn adds Saturn as a friend. Result: Sun, Moon, Jupiter are friends; Mercury is an enemy; Venus (friend and enemy) and Saturn (friend and enemy) cancel to neutral. That is exactly the table below. Run for all seven planets, the rule reproduces every row.

PlanetFriendsNeutralsEnemies
SunMoon, Mars, JupiterMercuryVenus, Saturn
MoonSun, MercuryMars, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn—
MarsSun, Moon, JupiterVenus, SaturnMercury
MercurySun, VenusMars, Jupiter, SaturnMoon
JupiterSun, Moon, MarsSaturnMercury, Venus
VenusMercury, SaturnMars, JupiterSun, Moon
SaturnMercury, VenusJupiterSun, Moon, Mars

Santhanam’s note on this verse adds that the Moon has no enemies, as in the Chaukhamba edition and in Saravali, and lists the nodes: Rahu friends Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, enemies Sun, Moon, Mars, neutral Mercury; Ketu friends Mars, Venus, Saturn, enemies the Sun and Moon, neutral Mercury and Jupiter. Treat the node rows as one author’s note, not a settled table.

Step 2: temporary friendship (this chart only)

BPHS ch. 3 verse 56: count from one planet to the other. If the other lies in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th, it is a temporary friend. In the 1st (same house), 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th or 9th, it is a temporary enemy. The rule is mutual: 2nd and 12th, 3rd and 11th, 4th and 10th pair up.

Notice that planets in the same house are temporary enemies, which surprises most beginners.

Step 3: combine into five grades

NaturalTemporaryResult (BPHS ch. 3 verses 57 to 58)
FriendFriendGreat friend (adhi mitra)
NeutralFriendFriend (mitra)
EnemyFriendNeutral (sama)
FriendEnemyNeutral (sama)
NeutralEnemyEnemy (shatru)
EnemyEnemyGreat enemy (adhi shatru)

The five grades are what Shadbala later scores as 20, 15, 10, 4 and 2 virupas for the planet’s sign in Santhanam’s rendering (lesson 4-1 gives the other common scale). Relationships are not always symmetric: A can be a friend of B while B is only neutral to A.

In your chart

The pairs below come from your own houses. Each row is read “first planet looks at the second”.

PairHousesNaturalTemporaryFive-fold
Mars sees Venus9 → 9 (the 1st)neutralenemyenemy
Venus sees Mars9 → 9 (the 1st)neutralenemyenemy
Mercury sees Jupiter10 → 7 (the 10th)neutralfriendfriend
Jupiter sees Mercury7 → 10 (the 4th)enemyfriendneutral
Sun sees Mercury10 → 10 (the 1st)neutralenemyenemy
Mercury sees Sun10 → 10 (the 1st)friendenemyneutral
Saturn sees Mercury8 → 10 (the 3rd)friendfriendgreat friend
Mercury sees Saturn10 → 8 (the 11th)neutralfriendfriend
Mars sees Sun9 → 10 (the 2nd)friendfriendgreat friend

Three things to see. First, Mars and Venus share your 9th house, so each counts the other a temporary enemy, and the natural neutrality becomes enmity in both directions. Second, Mercury (lagna lord) treats Jupiter (7th lord) as a friend, but Jupiter treats Mercury as only neutral; the relationship is lopsided. Third, Saturn sees Mercury as a great friend (natural friend plus temporary friend), while Mercury sees Saturn only as a friend (natural neutral plus temporary friend). That matters because Saturn is the running antardasha lord in Mercury’s mahadasha (Stage 5).

Now the sign each planet occupies:

PlanetSignNatural view of the sign lordFive-fold view
SunGemini (Mercury’s sign)neutralenemy
MoonCancer (own)——
MarsTaurus (Venus’s sign)neutralenemy
MercuryGemini (own)——
JupiterPisces (own)——
VenusTaurus (own)——
SaturnAries (Mars’s sign)enemyneutral

Compare Sun and Mars. By the natural table alone, both sit in a “neutral” sign. By the five-fold view, both sit in an enemy’s sign, because each shares a house with its host (Sun with Mercury, Mars with Venus), which makes them temporary enemies. The five-fold reading is the harsher and, per BPHS, the more complete one.

Where the schools differ
  • Parashari (BPHS): natural plus temporary, combined into five grades. Shadbala uses the combined grade.
  • Simple software labels: many programs, including this engine, label a planet’s sign friend, neutral or enemy using the natural table alone. That is faster but ignores your chart’s own geometry. Know which one a printout used before you compare two readings.
  • Edition differences: Santhanam notes that the Chaukhamba edition and Saravali agree the Moon has no enemy; some derived tables in circulation do not. Check the source of a table before trusting a Moon verdict.
  • Jaimini and KP: neither works from a friendship grid. Jaimini uses rashi aspects and karakas; KP uses the star lord and sub-lord.
Cross-check

Pick any planet and re-derive its row of the natural table with the verse-55 rule, as shown for Mars. If your derived row differs from a book’s row, the book is using a variant. Then count the temporary relationship from the houses, not from the signs: the signs can differ while the houses are the same.

Remember
  • Natural friendship is fixed; derive it with the verse-55 rule from the moolatrikona sign.
  • Temporary friendship: 2, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12 from each other = friend; 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 = enemy.
  • Combine: friend+friend = great friend, enemy+enemy = great enemy, friend with enemy = neutral.
  • Many software labels use the natural table only; the five-fold reading can be harsher.

Practice: Work out the five-fold relationship between your Moon and your Saturn, in both directions, and then between your Sun and your Moon. Note any asymmetry.
lessons.listen: Planetary friendship is measured twice. The natural friendship is fixed. Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra gives a rule that rebuilds the whole table: from a planet’s moolatrikona sign, the lords of the second, fourth, fifth, eighth, ninth and twelfth signs are friends, and the lords of the third, sixth, seventh, tenth and eleventh are enemies. The lord of its exaltation sign is always a friend, and anything counted both ways is neutral. The temporary friendship belongs to one chart: planets in the second, third, fourth, tenth, eleventh or twelfth from each other are friends, and in the first, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth or ninth they are enemies. Planets in the same house are temporary enemies. Combine the two into five grades, from great friend to great enemy. In your chart Mars and Venus, together in the ninth house, become enemies of each other. Mercury treats Jupiter as a friend, but Jupiter treats Mercury only as neutral. Many software labels use the natural table only, so know which one you are reading.
sources: BPHS ch. 3 (planetary characters and description), verse 55 on natural relationships, verse 56 on temporary relationships, verses 57 to 58 on the five-fold relationship; R. Santhanam’s translation and notes
BPHS ch. 27 (evaluation of strengths), verses 2 to 4 on the virupa values for friendship grades

quiz.q: Planets in the same house are, in temporary friendship, …
o: Friends only if both are benefics
quiz.w: The 1st (same house), 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th from each other are temporary enemy positions.

quiz.q: Natural friend + temporary enemy gives…
quiz.w: A friendship and an enmity cancel to neutral.

quiz.q: Which planet, by the natural table, has no enemies?
quiz.w: The Moon has friends Sun and Mercury and neutral for the rest; BPHS lists no enemy for her.

quiz.q: In your chart, Mars and Venus together in the 9th house are, in the five-fold relationship, …
quiz.w: Natural neutral plus temporary enemy (same house) gives enemy, in both directions.

quiz.q: In the verse-55 rule, how is the lord of a planet’s exaltation sign counted?
o: As one friend-count, which cancels to neutral if it also rules an enemy-position sign
Always as a great friend, whatever else it rules
It is left out of the count
quiz.w: Verse 55 adds the exaltation lord as a friend. If that planet also rules a 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th or 11th sign from the moolatrikona, the two counts cancel: Jupiter, lord of Venus’s exaltation sign Pisces, ends up neutral to Venus.

lessons.title: Combustion, planetary war and retrogression
lessons.body:
Recall: Mars and Venus share your 9th house. What is their five-fold relationship, and why?

A planet can be well placed by dignity and still be hindered by what is happening around it in the sky. Three conditions are classical: it can be burnt by the Sun ({{term:combust|combustion}}), it can lose a fight with another planet ({{term:grahayuddha|planetary war}}), or it can be moving backward ({{term:retrograde|retrograde}}). Each is a separate test.

1. Combustion (asta)

A planet within a set number of degrees of the Sun, measured along the zodiac, is called combust. Its light is “swallowed” and it loses independence. The conventional orbs, printed by Santhanam in his notes to BPHS ch. 7 (verses 28 and 29 speak of a planet at the same longitude as the Sun losing its strength):

PlanetOrb when directOrb when retrograde
Moon12°same
Mars17°same
Mercury14°12°
Jupiter11°same
Venus10°8°
Saturn15°same
  • Rahu and Ketu are never combust. They are points, not bodies, and in fact they eclipse the Sun.
  • Combustion lowers strength; it does not erase a planet. A combust planet in its own sign, exalted, or vargottama is usually judged less affected than a combust planet in an enemy’s sign.
  • The depth matters: 2° from the Sun is a very different condition from 16° from the Sun in Mars’s 17° orb.
In your chart

Your separations from the Sun, from the engine’s longitudes:

PlanetDistance from SunOrbVerdict
Moon27°23′12°free of the Sun
Mars11°22′17°combust
Mercury17°29′14°free of the Sun
Jupiter97°12′11°free of the Sun
Venus32°23′10°free of the Sun
Saturn62°59′15°free of the Sun

Mars is your one combust planet. It is 11°22′ from the Sun inside a 17° orb, which is 5°38′ inside the edge, about one-third of the way to exact conjunction. This is moderate, not extreme. Mars is also your Atmakaraka, the ruler of your 3rd and 8th houses, and it sits in Venus’s sign in the 9th. So three separate facts about Mars (combust, enemy’s sign by the five-fold test, functional malefic) all point the same way. That does not make Mars useless; it means its results arrive with the Sun’s themes mixed in, such as authority, father and ego.

Mercury is 17°29′ from the Sun, outside its 14° orb, so it is not combust even though it shares a sign with the Sun.

Where the schools differ
  • Do Venus and Saturn burn? Santhanam’s note under BPHS ch. 7 says yes: they lose their rays like the others, against the common belief that they are exempt. His notes on the longevity calculation in ch. 43 say the halving for combustion does not apply to Venus and Saturn. The same translator, two chapters, two answers. A teacher’s view on this is a convention, not a settled verse.
  • Orb sizes: software and almanacs differ a little in the orbs they use, particularly for Mercury and Venus when retrograde. Check the orb before you compare two printouts.

2. Planetary war (graha yuddha)

When two of the five star-planets (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) stand within 1° of longitude, they are said to be at war. The Sun and Moon are not part of it (a close Moon is a mere meeting) and the nodes do not take part. BPHS ch. 79 verse 9 (Santhanam’s numbering) states it: planetary war arises if Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn are within one degree; Venus is the winner whether north or south, and among the other four the planet in the north wins. The loser’s house suffers: BPHS ch. 11 (Santhanam’s notes) say a bhava’s potency is void if its planet is defeated in war, and BPHS ch. 27 verse 20 adds the difference of the two Shadbalas to the winner and subtracts it from the loser.

The texts disagree about who wins:

RuleWho holds itWinner
Northern planet wins; Venus always winsBPHS ch. 79 verse 9, as translated by SanthanamMore northerly planet; Venus regardless
Higher latitude (north) winsSurya Siddhanta tradition; also one modern author quoted by Santhanam, C. G. RajanPlanet with the higher northern celestial latitude
Brighter, larger-looking planet wins; Venus usually winsBrihat Samhita ch. 17, with commentaryJudged by size, brightness and shine
Smaller longitude winsSanthanam notes this is “normally taught” (BPHS ch. 11 note)Planet with the lesser longitude
In your chart

No two of your five star-planets are within 1° of each other, so you have no natal planetary war. The closest pair is Venus and Mars, about 21° apart. A transit example shows how the rules behave. Venus and Saturn meet in Pisces on 8 May 2027; the exact conjunction falls at about 00:20 IST, at Pisces 27°08′, and the two stay within 1° for roughly two days around it. Venus’s celestial latitude is −1.65° and Saturn’s −2.26°, so Venus is the more northerly. By the BPHS rule, the northern rule and the brightness rule, Venus wins. The smaller-longitude rule flips at the exact conjunction: before it Venus has the smaller longitude, after it Saturn does (at 06:00 IST Venus is at 27°26′ and Saturn at 27°10′, 0.26° apart), so that rule picks Saturn only after about 00:20. Because the rules split, treat any war verdict as one voice among several, and use it mainly in the natal chart.

Planetary war is a natal-chart and mundane idea. Do not build personal predictions on a transit war; use it only to explain why a particular planet may behave weakly in a natal chart.

3. Retrogression (vakri)

Retrograde motion is an apparent backward drift seen from Earth. The Sun and Moon never turn retrograde; the five star-planets do; the mean nodes always move backward. BPHS ch. 27 verses 21 to 23 list eight kinds of planetary motion and the cheshta bala (motional strength, in virupas) each earns:

MotionCheshta bala (virupas)
Vakra (retrograde)60
Anuvakra (entering the previous sign while retrograde)30
Vikala (stationary)15
Manda (slower than usual)30
Mandatara (slower still)15
Sama (a little faster than manda)7.5
Chara (fast)45
Atichara (entering the next sign at speed)30

The maximum, 60, goes to a retrograde planet. In the BPHS Shadbala scheme a retrograde planet is therefore strong. The same author, in the longevity chapter, exempts a retrograde planet from the one-third reduction that applies to a planet in an enemy’s sign, using the word “vakrachara”.

Where the schools differ
  • BPHS (Shadbala, ch. 27 and ch. 43): retrograde means strong; maximum motional strength; no enemy-sign reduction.
  • Exaltation reversal: secondary sources attribute to Phaladeepika and Uttara Kalamrita the view that a retrograde planet in a debilitation sign acts as if exalted, and a retrograde planet in an exaltation sign acts as if debilitated. These are reported in secondary summaries; the verses have not been checked for this course, so treat this as reported, not verified.
  • Saravali: reported to say that retrograde benefics bring good and retrograde malefics bring trouble. Same caveat.
  • Modern practice: retrograde planets are often described as delayed, inward or “revisiting” in their results. This is a modern gloss, not a classical rule.
  • Timing inside a dasha (BPHS ch. 47): a retrograde planet’s results come in the reverse order of the decanate rule you will meet in Stage 5.
In your chart

At birth all seven of your planets were direct. Jupiter turned retrograde about 22 days after you were born (18 July 1998, at Pisces 4°13′) and Saturn about 51 days after (16 August 1998 IST, at Aries 9°48′). So neither was retrograde in your chart; the dates are useful only as a reminder that both were still moving forward. Rahu and Ketu are always shown moving backward; the engine uses mean nodes.

Cross-check

Re-run your combustion list with a wider and a narrower orb, for example 10° and 17° for Mars. Your Mars is combust at 17° but not at 10°. A call that depends on the orb is a soft call. Then note what the Sun-Mars separation is under another ayanamsa: it does not change, because both planets shift together. Combustion is therefore stable across ayanamsas; only the choice of orb can alter it.

Remember
  • Combustion orbs: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° retrograde), Saturn 15°.
  • Planetary war needs two of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn within 1°; the rules for the winner differ by text.
  • In BPHS Shadbala, a retrograde planet is strong, 60 virupas of cheshta bala.
  • Your only combust planet is Mars, about 11°22′ from the Sun.

Practice: List the angular distance of Mars from the Sun under three orb choices (10°, 14°, 17°). Then write a two-line statement of what “combust Mars” does and does not change about your 3rd and 8th houses.
lessons.listen: Three conditions can weaken a planet that looks well placed. First, combustion: a planet too close to the Sun loses independence. The orbs are Moon twelve degrees, Mars seventeen, Mercury fourteen or twelve when retrograde, Jupiter eleven, Venus ten or eight when retrograde, and Saturn fifteen. Rahu and Ketu are never combust. In your chart only Mars is combust, about eleven degrees from the Sun. Mercury is seventeen and a half degrees away and is free. Second, planetary war: when two of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn stand within one degree, one is judged the winner. Brihat Parashara says the northern planet wins, and Venus wins whichever side it stands. Other texts use brightness, and some teachers use the smaller longitude. You have no planetary war at birth. Third, retrogression: in the Shadbala scheme of Parashara a retrograde planet earns the maximum sixty virupas of motional strength, so it counts as strong. Other texts, reported in secondary sources, reverse exaltation and fall for retrograde planets. All seven of your planets were direct at birth.

lessons.title: Functional benefics and malefics for each lagna
lessons.body:
Recall: Which of your planets is combust, and by roughly how many degrees is it inside its orb?

Stage 1 gave you the natural nature of the planets: Jupiter and Venus benefic, Saturn and Mars malefic. Natural nature is the planet’s habit. {{term:functional|Functional nature}} is its job in your chart, and it depends on which houses the planet rules for your lagna. A natural benefic can be a functional malefic, and the reverse. Parashari astrology judges a planet by its functional role first.

The principles (BPHS ch. 34, verses 2 to 7, with Santhanam’s notes)

  • The lords of the trikonas (5th and 9th) are auspicious. They are the main givers of wealth and fortune. The lagna lord is specially auspicious, since the lagna is both kendra and trikona.
  • The lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th are inauspicious. The lords of the 2nd, 8th and 12th act according to their company and their other house. The 8th lordship of the Sun and Moon is not evil.
  • A natural benefic ruling a kendra takes the blemish called {{term:kendradhipati|kendradhipati}}. Santhanam’s note ranks the blemish in ascending order Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus. The lagna lord is excused.
  • A natural malefic ruling a kendra is not harmful but not helpful either, unless it also rules a trikona. Then it is a {{term:yogakaraka|yogakaraka}}.
  • A moolatrikona lordship outweighs a plain own-sign lordship. When a planet rules one good and one evil house, the stronger of the two prevails.
  • The 9th and 10th lords are the best planets for any lagna; the 11th and 8th lords the most adverse in their groups.

BPHS then goes lagna by lagna (ch. 34 verses 19 to 44) and names the auspicious planets, the malefics and the marakas. Santhanam notes that the sage often skips a planet whose role is mixed.

All twelve lagnas

LagnaYogakaraka (kendra + trikona lord)BPHS ch. 34: auspiciousBPHS ch. 34: malefic2nd and 7th lords (maraka)

The yogakaraka and maraka columns are derived from the lordships; the two BPHS columns follow verses 19 to 44 as Santhanam renders them. A planet missing from both BPHS columns is one the verse leaves unmentioned (for example the Moon for Aries, Saturn for Gemini and Virgo). Where your lagna’s row says “none”, no single planet rules both a kendra and a trikona; the texts then name pairs, such as Mercury with Venus for Virgo, Sun with Moon for Scorpio, Mars with Jupiter for Pisces.

Maraka: a careful word

BPHS ch. 44 verses 2 to 5: the 3rd and 8th are the houses of longevity; the 12th from each, the 2nd and 7th, are the maraka houses, and their lords (and malefics in them) are marakas. Santhanam’s own note on the chapter warns that saying “the 2nd lord’s dasha will bring death” is a misnomer; lifespan must be judged through the longevity methods. Read maraka as “strain on vitality and energy in that planet’s periods”, not as a prediction of danger.

In your chart

Your lagna is Virgo (highlighted row). The BPHS verdict for each of your planets:

PlanetRulesFunctional role (Virgo)Where it sits
Mercury1, 10Auspicious: lagna lord, excused from kendradhipatiGemini 28°10′, 10th

Saturn5, 6Not named by BPHS for Virgo; mixed: 5th trikona and friend of the lagna lord, but its moolatrikona sign Aquarius is your 6thAries 7°41′, 8th, debilitated
Moon11Malefic by BPHS (11th lord)Cancer 8°04′, 11th
Sun12Depends on association (BPHS)Gemini 10°41′, 10th, with Mercury
Rahu—Acts through its dispositor (the Sun) and any conjunctionLeo 10°33′, 12th

What this means. Two of your own-sign planets, Jupiter (own sign, kendra, Hamsa yoga) and the Moon (own sign), are both functional malefics for Virgo. A strong functional malefic is strong, but what it brings has a demanding or mixed character. Your two functional benefics, Mercury and Venus, are both in own sign and in houses of strength (10th and 9th). That is a good foundation. Note also that the engine lists “kendradhipati dosha” for Jupiter (ruler of the 4th and 7th), which matches BPHS naming Jupiter a malefic for Virgo. It does not flag Mercury, and Mercury, as lagna lord, would be excused anyway.

Where the schools differ
  • BPHS verse list: the table above, as translated by Santhanam. Santhanam notes the Susloka Sataka disagrees with BPHS about Venus for Taurus (the 6th lordship), and that Parasara’s word carries more weight for him.
  • Rule-based derivations: many textbooks and popular tables derive benefic and malefic lists purely from lordship rules (trikona lords good, 3rd 6th 11th lords bad). They agree with BPHS in most cells but differ where BPHS is silent or mixed. One popular online table, for example, lists Mercury as a benefic for Gemini, which BPHS does not state.
  • Jaimini: works from karakas and rashi aspects, not from lagna-wise benefic lists.
  • KP: judges a planet by the houses its star lord and sub-lord signify; it does not use the Parashari lagna-wise list.
Cross-check

Pick any planet in your chart and ask it three questions: what does BPHS ch. 34 say for my lagna; what do the lordship rules alone say; what does its dignity say? If the first two agree and the third is strong, the planet’s role is clear. If they disagree (Jupiter for Virgo: natural benefic, functional malefic, strong dignity), write the disagreement down rather than forcing a verdict.

Remember
  • Functional nature comes from lordship for your lagna; natural nature is only the habit.
  • Yogakaraka = one planet ruling a kendra and a trikona: Saturn for Taurus and Libra, Mars for Cancer and Leo, Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius.
  • Natural benefics ruling kendras take the kendradhipati blemish; the lagna lord is excused.
  • For Virgo: Mercury and Venus auspicious; Mars, Jupiter, Moon malefic; Venus doubles as a maraka lord.

Practice: Make a one-line card for each of your nine planets: natural nature, functional role for Virgo, house and dignity. Mark the two that disagree most between natural and functional nature.
lessons.listen: Natural nature is a planet’s habit. Functional nature is its job in your own chart, decided by the houses it rules for your lagna. Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, chapter thirty four, gives the principles. Lords of the fifth and ninth are auspicious, and the lagna lord is special. Lords of the third, sixth and eleventh are inauspicious. Natural benefics ruling a kendra take the kendradhipati blemish, but the lagna lord is excused. A planet that rules both a kendra and a trikona is a yogakaraka: Saturn for Taurus and Libra, Mars for Cancer and Leo, Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius. The second and seventh lords are the marakas, but that word means strain on vitality in their periods, not a prediction of danger. For your Virgo lagna, Mercury and Venus are the auspicious planets, and Mars, Jupiter and the Moon are malefic. Your Jupiter and Moon are strong in own sign yet functionally malefic, so they are strong but demanding. The engine flags kendradhipati dosha for Jupiter, the ruler of your fourth and seventh, not for Mercury, which as lagna lord is excused.

lessons.title: Aspects: graha drishti and Jaimini rashi drishti
lessons.body:
Recall: Your Mercury is the lagna lord and also the 10th lord. Is it excused from kendradhipati dosha, and why?

A planet influences more than the house it sits in. It also looks at other houses, and that look carries its nature there. Two systems of looking are used, and they give different answers for the same chart. Learn both, and note which one a writer is using.

1. Parashari graha drishti

This aspect is counted in houses, from the planet’s own house as the 1st. BPHS ch. 26 verses 1 to 5 (Santhanam’s numbering): the aspects on the 3rd and 10th, the 5th and 9th, the 4th and 8th, and lastly the 7th rise “in slabs of quarters”, a quarter, a half, three-quarters and full. All planets see the 7th house fully. Saturn, Jupiter and Mars have special aspects.

PlanetHouses aspected (counting itself as 1st)Classical strength (BPHS ch. 26)
Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus7thFull
Mars4th, 7th, 8thBPHS 26.2–5 grades the 4th and 8th at three-quarters in its slab scheme, yet names them Mars’s special aspects; most teachers today count them as full
Jupiter5th, 7th, 9thBPHS grades the 5th and 9th at one-half in its slab scheme, yet names them Jupiter’s special aspects; most teachers today count them as full
Saturn3rd, 7th, 10thBPHS grades the 3rd and 10th at one-quarter in its slab scheme, yet names them Saturn’s special aspects; most teachers today count them as full
Rahu, KetuEngine: 5th, 7th, 9thDisputed (see below)

The same chapter, right after these verses, gives a degree-based method: the aspect value depends on the angular distance, so an aspect can be partial even if the sign positions line up. In everyday work most people count houses only.

2. Jaimini rashi drishti

BPHS ch. 8 verses 1 to 3 gives the sign aspects, and Santhanam’s note says the same system came to be called Jaimini’s although Parashara taught it first. A planet casts the aspect of the sign it stands in. Degrees do not matter.

Sign typeSignsAspects
Movable (chara)Aries, Cancer, Libra, CapricornThe three fixed signs, except the fixed sign next to it
Fixed (sthira)Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, AquariusThe three movable signs, except the movable sign next to it
Dual (dwiswabhava)Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, PiscesThe other three dual signs

Check by hand: Aries (movable) does not look at Taurus, the adjacent fixed sign, but looks at Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius. Taurus (fixed) looks at Cancer, Libra and Capricorn, not Aries. Gemini (dual) looks at Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces. This is exactly the BPHS example.

In your chart

Both systems for your nine planets, from the engine’s positions. Occupants are in brackets.

PlanetSign (house)Parashari: houses aspectedJaimini: signs aspected

MoonCancer (11th)5thTaurus (9th) [Mars, Venus], Scorpio (3rd), Aquarius (6th) [Ketu]

MercuryGemini (10th)4thVirgo (1st), Sagittarius (4th), Pisces (7th) [Jupiter]

KetuAquarius (6th)10th (Sun, Mercury), 12th (Rahu), 2ndAries (8th) [Saturn], Cancer (11th) [Moon], Libra (2nd)

Where they disagree on your chart:

  • Jupiter in Pisces looks at your Moon in the 11th by Parashari rules (its 5th aspect). By Jaimini rules Pisces is dual and looks at Gemini, Virgo and Sagittarius, so Jupiter looks at your Sun and Mercury in the 10th instead, and at the lagna. Both systems agree Jupiter looks at your lagna.
  • Saturn in Aries looks at your Sun and Mercury in the 10th in the Parashari system (its 3rd aspect: Gemini is the 3rd sign from Aries). Jaimini’s Aries looks at Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius, which holds Rahu and Ketu, not the 10th.
  • Mars and Venus in Taurus look at the Moon in Cancer only in the Jaimini system. Mars’s Parashari aspects (12th, 3rd, 4th) miss the Moon in the 11th.
  • Your Moon looks at Mars and Venus in the 9th by Jaimini rules (Cancer sees Taurus), and the Parashari 7th aspect of the Moon falls on an empty 5th house.

So your 10th house is looked at by Saturn in one system and by Jupiter in the other. That is a real difference in reading, not a detail.

Where the schools differ
  • Rahu and Ketu: BPHS as translated by Santhanam does not list the nodes among the planets with special aspects in ch. 26, though a note in ch. 3 argues that Rahu clearly has aspects. In practice some teachers give the nodes only the 7th, others the 5th, 7th and 9th (as the engine does), and some say nodes aspect nothing. Test each version on your own chart before trusting any.
  • Jaimini: sign aspects only, by sign; a planet’s aspect is the sign’s aspect. Parashari authors use both systems side by side, with graha drishti as the main one.
  • KP: works through star lord and sub lord significators and uses aspects very little.
  • Tajika: has its own orb-based aspects for the annual chart. They belong to the Varshaphala stage and are not taught here.
Cross-check

For any aspect you want to rely on, check it in three ways. First, count in houses (Parashari). Second, check the signs (Jaimini). Third, ask whether the aspecting planet is strong in the D9. An aspect that appears in only one system should be written as a note, not a conclusion. Also try birth time minus five minutes: aspects by house do not change, but a lagna at a sign edge can shift every house count.

Remember
  • Parashari aspects are counted by houses: all see the 7th; Mars 4/8, Jupiter 5/9, Saturn 3/10.
  • Jaimini aspects are by sign type: movable sees fixed, fixed sees movable (except the adjacent), dual sees dual.
  • The two systems give different answers on your chart for the 10th house and the Moon.
  • Aspects of Rahu and Ketu are disputed, so list them as optional.

Practice: Pick your 10th house. Write which planets look at it in the Parashari system and which in the Jaimini system. Then write one sentence on how you would phrase a reading that survives both.
lessons.listen: A planet affects the houses it looks at as well as the one it sits in. Parashari aspect, or graha drishti, is counted in houses. Every planet sees the seventh house. Mars also sees the fourth and eighth, Jupiter the fifth and ninth, Saturn the third and tenth. In chapter twenty six Parashara grades these in quarters, a quarter, a half, three quarters and full. Jaimini sign aspect, or rashi drishti, is also in Brihat Parashara chapter eight. Movable signs see the fixed signs except the adjacent one. Fixed signs see the movable signs except the adjacent one. Dual signs see the other dual signs. Degrees do not matter. On your chart the two systems disagree. Jupiter looks at your Moon by Parashari rules but at your Sun and Mercury in the tenth by Jaimini rules. Saturn looks at your tenth by Parashari rules only. Mars and Venus look at your Moon only by Jaimini rules. The aspects of Rahu and Ketu are disputed, so treat them as optional. When two systems disagree, write the point as a note and test it against real events in your ledger.

lessons.title: House lords in houses: the principles
lessons.body:
Recall: Which planet rules your 4th and 7th houses, and where does it sit?

Every house has a lord ({{term:bhavesha|bhavesha}}), the planet ruling the sign on that house. The lord carries the house’s subject to wherever it sits. If your 10th lord is in the 12th, the career themes go to the 12th. The question is always: what does the lord bring, where does it take it, and in what condition?

A four-question routine

  1. What does the house stand for? The 10th is career and public work; the 12th is loss, expense, seclusion and foreign lands.
  2. Where is its lord? The house the lord is in becomes the place where the first house’s matters play out.
  3. How strong is the lord? Look at dignity, combustion, the navamsa, and who joins or looks at it.
  4. What else does the lord rule? A planet with two houses mixes two results.

BPHS ch. 24 verses 145 to 148 (Santhanam’s numbering) states the same ideas: the effects of house lords are to be deduced by considering strengths and weaknesses; a planet owning two houses gives results for both lordships; contrary results neutralise, different results are both seen; and the planet yields full, half or a quarter of its effect according to being strong, medium or negligible. Chapter 24 gives a verse for each lord in each house, 144 in all, and Santhanam’s notes keep adding qualifiers.

Where the lord falls from its own house

A common working method counts the distance from the house to the lord’s position. It is a modern synthesis of classical ideas, so treat it as a guide, not a verse.

Lord sits in the … from its own houseUsual reading
1st (the same house)Strong; the house’s matters are self-supported
2nd, 3rd, 11thSupportive; good effort and gain
4th, 7th, 10thActive; the house gets drive and visibility
5th, 9thFortunate, protected by merit
6th, 8th, 12thStrained; the matters of the house meet obstacles, delay or loss. When the lord is itself the lord of the 6th, 8th or 12th, the viparita rules may reverse this.

Worked examples: the 12th lord and the 10th house

The table follows BPHS ch. 24 as Santhanam renders it, in short paraphrase. The verses are stark, so treat each as one tendency whose strength depends on the planet’s condition. They are not a prediction for any one person.

PlacementBPHS ch. 24How to carry it
Lagna lord in the 10thVerse 10: paternal happiness, royal honour, fame and self-earned wealthSelf and career fuse. The person works in the public eye and builds through his own effort.
10th lord in the 10thVerse 118: skilful in all jobs, valorous, truthful and devoted to eldersThe strongest case for a career house: the lord is at home.
10th lord in the 12thVerse 120: expense through royal abodes (authority, government), fear of enemies, anxiety despite skillSanthanam reads it as cost through taxes, fines and political spending. Career can run abroad or behind the scenes. Modern readers add foreign work and institutions.
12th lord in the 10thVerse 142: expense through royal persons, only moderate paternal happinessExpense and loss themes attach to career and authority. Can also mean working in hospitals, ashrams, foreign firms or behind-the-scenes roles.
In your chart

Three of these are on your chart at the same time:

  • Lagna lord in the 10th (verse 10). Mercury, lord of Virgo, sits in Gemini 28°10′ in the 10th. It is in its own sign and vargottama, so this placement is as strong as Mercury can make it.
  • 10th lord in the 10th (verse 118). The same Mercury, as 10th lord. It is both lagna lord and 10th lord, so your self and your career run through one planet.
  • 12th lord in the 10th (verse 142). The Sun, lord of Leo (12th), also sits in Gemini, 10°41′, in the 10th, 17°29′ from Mercury, outside Mercury’s combustion orb. Verse 142 reads it as expense through authority and moderate paternal happiness. The Sun in the 10th also has directional strength (dig bala), so the Sun is not weak here.

Putting them together: your career house has two lords of different kinds in it, an excellent one (Mercury) and one that brings the “spend, give away, work behind” colour (the Sun). Do not choose one verse and ignore the others. Read the whole bundle, and log specific predictions in your ledger so you can see over time which part shows up.

Where the schools differ
  • BPHS ch. 24: a verse for each lord in each house, with the principles in verses 145 to 148. Santhanam’s notes add that some results hold only for particular lagnas.
  • Phaladeepika and Saravali: give house-lord results in a similar scheme; the details differ in places. Their chapter numbers have not been verified, so the lesson does not cite them.
  • Jaimini: reads the lord by its sign and its aspects, not by distance from the house.
  • KP: reads the house through the star lord and sub lord of its cusp, not the sign lord alone.

The classical verses use words like “bereft”, “sinful” and “poverty”. Read them as the text’s way of marking an unsupported placement, not as a verdict on a person. A placement describes a pull. The lord’s dignity, aspects, the dasha running and your own choices decide what happens. Log any prediction you draw in your prediction ledger with a window and a result.

Cross-check

Pick one house lord and test it three ways: the verse (BPHS ch. 24), the distance method above, and the D9 position of the lord. If the three agree, state the result firmly. If they split, call it mixed and say which part you trust more and why.

Remember
  • Four questions: what the house stands for; where its lord sits; how strong the lord is; what else it rules.
  • BPHS ch. 24 verses 145 to 148: judge by strength; two lordships give two sets of results; the planet gives full, half or a quarter.
  • Lord in own house is strongest; 6th, 8th and 12th from its own house is strained.
  • On your chart the 10th has two lords of different kinds: Mercury (strong) and the Sun (12th lord).

Practice: Write the BPHS ch. 24 verse number and a one-line paraphrase for your 2nd lord, 4th lord and 7th lord. Then write whether the lord’s dignity raises or lowers each reading.
lessons.listen: Every house has a lord, and the lord carries the house’s subject to wherever it sits. Ask four questions. What does the house stand for? Where is its lord? How strong is the lord? lessons.title: Judge your 12 house lords
lessons.body:
Recall: Name the BPHS ch. 24 verse you would use for the 12th lord in the 10th, and what it says in one line.

You now have the tools for each step: dignity (4-1), friendship (4-2), combustion (4-3), functional nature (4-4), aspects (4-5) and house-lord principles (4-6). This lesson puts them together on all twelve of your lords. The help is removed in three stages.

The five steps

  1. Name the house’s themes.
  2. Locate its lord and say what the placement means.
  3. Judge the lord’s condition: dignity, five-fold friendship, combustion, D9.
  4. Note who joins or looks at the lord.
  5. Write a verdict: strong, mixed or strained, with one line on why.

Stage A: fully worked (houses 1 to 4)

Judge the planet’s condition once and then say what each house gets from it. Verdicts here are tendencies to be tested in your ledger, not facts about outcomes.

Where the schools differ
  • Debilitated Saturn: the engine lists two cancellation candidates; other rule sets accept or reject each. Hold the Saturn verdict as “mixed, with support”, not settled.
  • Combust Mars: if you use a smaller orb, Mars is not combust and the verdict for houses 3 and 8 moves up a step.
  • Dignity labels: the engine marks Mars “neutral” in Taurus by natural friendship only. The five-fold test makes it an enemy sign, which is what the verdict uses.

  • Judge a planet once, then read each house it rules.
  • Stronger lords on your chart: Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Moon.
  • Strained lords: Mars (combust, enemy sign) and Saturn (debilitated, with cancellation candidates).
  • Verdicts are tendencies. Log them and check against what happens.

lessons.title: Synthesis: your planetary dossier and stage test
lessons.body:
Recall: Which two of your planets are weakest by dignity and condition, and what rule set makes one of them better?

This lesson turns the stage into a single page about your chart, then tests you. The page is your planetary dossier: for every planet, its dignity, condition, functional nature and the houses it rules. It is the reference you will use in the timing lessons that follow.

Your seven-planet dossier

Rahu is in Leo in the 12th and Ketu in Aquarius in the 6th. The nodes take the results of their sign lord (the Sun and Saturn) and of any planet joined to them, which is why a dossier lists them last.

In your chart

Read the table as a chart story.

  • Strongest planets: Mercury (lagna and 10th lord, own sign, vargottama, in the 10th), then Venus and Jupiter, each in own sign, and the Moon. All four are on the functional side of the ledger in different ways: Mercury and Venus are functional benefics for Virgo, while Jupiter and the Moon are functional malefics, so Jupiter and the Moon are strong yet demanding.
  • Weak links: Mars (combust, enemy’s sign, rules 3rd and 8th) and Saturn (debilitated, rules 5th and 6th, lifted by cancellation candidates and Harsha).
  • The big picture: your 10th house carries Mercury and the Sun, your 9th carries Venus and Mars, and your 7th carries Jupiter. Four planets in the 9th and 10th houses mean your life energy is weighted towards fortune, work and public life.
  • Dasha link: you are in the Mercury major period, which is the planet with the highest grade in your dossier. You will use that in Stage 5.
Where the schools differ
  • Grades are this course’s summary, not a classical scale. The grades summarise this stage’s tests. BPHS uses Shadbala and Ashtavarga numbers for strength; a Shadbala scale would reorder some planets.
  • If your teacher uses a different orb, a different cancellation rule set, or treats Rahu and Ketu differently, the grades for Mars, Saturn and the nodes may shift.
Cross-check

Compare this table with the strength figures from a Shadbala printout, and with the Ashtakavarga tables in the engine. Differences are not errors. They show which strength you are measuring. Where all three agree on a planet, trust it most.

Remember
  • Strong and weak planets by dignity: Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Moon strong; Mars and Saturn weak.
  • Judge a planet by dignity, condition, functional nature and houses, in that order.
  • Rahu and Ketu act through their sign lords and companions.
  • A dossier is a reference, not a forecast. Predictions go into your ledger with dates.

Practice: Copy the dossier into your own notebook. Add a column “what I will test” for each planet, with one observable fact from your life that would support or contradict its grade.

Stage test

Take the seven questions below at the end of the page. Use the dossier above, and the earlier lessons if you need to, but answer each from reasoning before you check.
